Body: You already know what it feels like when your jacket fails mid-route. Water working through the seams, that clammy layer building up inside — it pulls your focus off the trail and onto your gear, which is exactly where it shouldn't be.

The Northbay Stormline Shell Jacket (NB-JKT-07) is built for sustained wet weather. Here's what that means in concrete terms:

- 20,000mm waterproof rating — holds up in heavy, prolonged rain
- 20,000 g/m² breathability — moves moisture out when you're working hard on the ascent
- 3-layer laminate construction — the face fabric, membrane, and backer are bonded together, so there's no inner lining to trap heat or sag when wet
- 420g total weight — light enough to carry without noticing it on a clear morning

This is a shell, not an insulated jacket. It won't keep you warm on its own in cold conditions — layer underneath for that. What it does is keep the weather out and let your body breathe while you move.

If your trips take you into the kind of terrain where the forecast is more suggestion than fact, this jacket was designed for exactly those days.
